items.title: The Mexican Drought Atlas: Tree-ring reconstructions of the soil moisture balance during the late pre-Hispanic, colonial, and modern eras
items.note: Gridded soil-moisture reconstructions for Mexico from 1400 CE, letting drought in the 1540s and 1570s be mapped against epidemic reports year by year.

items.title: Nahua and Spanish Concepts of Health and Disease in Colonial Mexico, 1519-1615
items.note: Compares Nahua and Spanish understandings of health and disease from conquest to 1615, the conceptual frame for reading epidemic names such as cocoliztli.

items.title: Salmonella enterica genomes recovered from victims of a major 16th century epidemic in Mexico
items.note: Preprint of the Teposcolula Yucundaa study, which drew wide press coverage and early criticism that the method could not detect RNA viruses.

items.title: A través de sus ojos: médicos indígenas y el cocoliztli de 1545 en la Nueva España
items.note: Examines how Indigenous physicians perceived and treated the 1545 cocoliztli, arguing the disease category was socially constructed across Nahua and Spanish medicine.

items.title: Salmonella enterica genomes from victims of a major sixteenth-century epidemic in Mexico
items.note: Recovered Salmonella enterica Paratyphi C genomes from burials at Teposcolula Yucundaa, proposing enteric fever as a candidate cause of the 1545 epidemic without excluding other pathogens.

items.title: Pan-genome Analysis of Ancient and Modern Salmonella enterica Demonstrates Genomic Stability of the Invasive Para C Lineage for Millennia
items.note: A Paratyphi C genome from a c. 1200 CE Norwegian burial placed the lineage in medieval Europe, consistent with a European introduction to Mexico.

items.title: Cold Tropical Pacific Sea Surface Temperatures During the Late Sixteenth-Century North American Megadrought
items.note: Reconstructs persistent La Niña-like conditions in 1566–1590 as a likely driver of the megadrought that the drought-and-rodent hypothesis links to the 1576 epidemic.

items.title: Genomic Insights into Pre- and Post-Contact Human Pathogens in the New World
items.note: Dissertation setting out the Teposcolula pathogen screening and the MALT-based workflow used to identify Paratyphi C, with discussion of its limits.

items.title: The Mexican Mission: Indigenous Reconstruction and Mendicant Enterprise in New Spain, 1521–1600
items.note: Its chapter 'Hecatomb' uses viceregal civil records to trace the demographic crises of 1575–1595, in which at least 40 percent of the Indigenous population died.

items.title: Origin and Health Status of First-Generation Africans from Early Colonial Mexico
items.note: Genomes, isotopes and pathogen DNA (yaws, hepatitis B) from a sixteenth-century mass burial at the San José de los Naturales hospital, showing which pathogens such contexts can yield.

items.title: Changes in indigenous dress and the cocoliztli epidemic of 1544–1548 in New Spain
items.who: O. R. Benavides Cárabes and C. Viesca Treviño
items.note: Proposes that colonial changes in Indigenous clothing and living conditions favoured louse-borne transmission, reviving a typhus-related interpretation.

items.title: The Church of the Dead: The Epidemic of 1576 and the Birth of Christianity in the Americas
items.note: Religious history of the 1576 epidemic and its aftermath, centring Indigenous survivors and drawing on mendicant and Nahua sources.

items.title: Salmonella enterica from a soldier from the 1652 siege of Barcelona (Spain) supports historical transatlantic epidemic contacts
items.note: A seventeenth-century Paratyphi C genome from Barcelona clusters with the Mexican ones, which the authors read as support for transatlantic movement of the lineage.

items.title: La epidemia de cocoliztli (1576) en el teatro de Fernán González de Eslava
items.note: Reads the coloquios of González de Eslava as a contemporary literary witness to the 1576 epidemic in Mexico City.

items.title: Digital Florentine Codex
items.who: Getty Research Institute and Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana
items.note: Full online edition with searchable Nahuatl and Spanish transcriptions and new translations of Sahagún's codex, compiled during and after the 1576 epidemic.

items.title: Religion over Life and Death. The Cocoliztli in the Florentine Codex
items.note: Studies how the Florentine Codex presents the cocoliztli and frames its meaning in religious terms.

items.title: Evolutionary history and recurrent host adaptation in ancient Salmonella enterica
items.note: Fifty-three ancient Salmonella genomes from Eurasia (3500 BCE–1300 CE) reconstruct the Paratyphi C lineage's history, the background for any European-origin argument.

items.title: Ancient genomic insights into Salmonella enterica Paratyphi C from Central Mexico
items.note: A nineteenth-century Paratyphi C genome from Mexico City clusters with Teposcolula, read as colonial-era introduction followed by local persistence (not yet peer reviewed).
